bifrost: springboard/sdk/src/workspace.rs (app lifecycle), springboard/sdk/src/fswatch.rs (file change events), springboard/src/bare/docbroker.rs (file grants), springboard/src/bare/app_policy.rs (launch-time sandbox)
summary: BifrOSt has no system security event client. Its app lifecycle notifications and inotify-based file watching cover a small part of what Endpoint Security reports, and none of the authorization (allow or deny before an event happens) or kernel-level event types exist.

features.apple: es_new_client, es_delete_client, es_new_client_result_t (Creating a Client, Destroying a Client)
features.note: Wave 5 (w5-endpoint-security, parity/integration 93f283b0): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. No root-level client that connects to a monitoring subsystem. Apps only get the per-app control socket (springboard/sdk/src/control.rs).

features.apple: es_subscribe, es_unsubscribe, es_unsubscribe_all, es_subscriptions, es_event_type_t (Subscribing to Events)
features.note: Wave 2 (theme-20, parity/integration e52c2fd0): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. Nothing to subscribe to. The only event feeds are the workspace notifications and the file watcher, each with its own API.

features.feature: Process execution, fork and exit events
features.apple: es_event_exec_t, es_event_fork_t, es_event_exit_t, es_exec_arg, es_exec_env, es_exec_fd (Process Event Types)
features.note: Only app launch and terminate, emitted by the shell for its own apps. No arguments, environment, file descriptors, parent chain or processes outside the shell.

features.feature: Process signal, working directory and root directory events
features.note: Wave 2 (theme-20, parity/integration e52c2fd0): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. No hook on signal delivery or directory changes.

features.feature: File-system events (open, create, write, rename, unlink, and others)
features.apple: es_event_open_t, es_event_create_t, es_event_write_t, es_event_rename_t, es_event_unlink_t and the other File-System Event Types
features.note: Recursive inotify watch with events coalesced per path. Reports changes after they happen and gives no process that made the change. The docs name it FSEventStream in bifrost_app::fsevents, but the file is fswatch.rs. Docs and code disagree on the name.

features.feature: File metadata events (xattr, ACL, flags, mode, owner, stat, readdir)
features.apple: es_event_getextattr_t, es_event_setacl_t, es_event_stat_t, es_event_readdir_t and the other File Metadata Event Types
features.note: Wave 3 (w3-endpoint-security, parity/integration cf8e852d): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. The watcher reports content changes only, not attribute or metadata access.

features.apple: es_respond_auth_result, es_respond_flags_result, es_auth_result_t, AUTH event types, es_result_t
features.note: Wave 3 (w3-endpoint-security, parity/integration cf8e852d): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. Endpoint Security can allow or deny an operation before it runs. Docbroker grants decide what an app may open, but they are not a system event hook. The sandbox is applied once at launch with no per-event decision.

features.apple: es_event_mount_t, es_event_unmount_t, es_event_remount_t, ES_MOUNT_DISPOSITION_* (File System Mounting Event Types)
features.note: Wave 2 (theme-20, parity/integration e52c2fd0): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. The installer mounts and unmounts its own targets (springboard/src/installer/plan.rs). No API reports mounts to apps.
Wave 5 (theme-16, parity/integration 93f283b0): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. No hook on mmap or mprotect.

features.feature: Interprocess events (trace, remote thread creation, suspend and resume)
features.note: Wave 2 (theme-20, parity/integration e52c2fd0): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. No ptrace or remote-thread monitoring found in springboard/src, springboard/sdk/src or springboard/core/src.

features.feature: Task port events (get task, read, inspect, name ports)
features.apple: es_event_get_task_t, es_event_get_task_read_t, es_event_get_task_inspect_t, es_event_get_task_name_t (Task Port Event Types)
features.note: Mach task ports are the macOS kernel IPC model. Linux has no equivalent, so there is no counterpart to monitor.

features.feature: User and group ID change events
features.apple: es_event_setuid_t, es_event_setgid_t, es_event_seteuid_t, es_event_setegid_t, es_event_setreuid_t, es_event_setregid_t (User and Group ID Types)
features.note: Wave 3 (w3-endpoint-security, parity/integration cf8e852d): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. No hook on credential changes. Launch-time identity drops are handled in springboard/src/bare/app_policy.rs (drop_identity), with no event emitted.

Wave 3 (theme-28, parity/integration cf8e852d): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. No code-signing status events. Packages are checked at install time, which is a different event.

features.feature: Login, logout, su, sudo, SSH and screen-sharing events
features.apple: ES_EVENT_TYPE_NOTIFY_LOGIN_LOGIN, ES_EVENT_TYPE_NOTIFY_SUDO, ES_EVENT_TYPE_NOTIFY_OPENSSH_LOGIN, ES_EVENT_TYPE_NOTIFY_SCREENSHARING_ATTACH and related notify types
features.note: Wave 5 (w5-endpoint-security, parity/integration 93f283b0): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. Session events are not published to apps. Logs go to the journal, and no security event stream is built from them.

features.feature: Socket, pseudoterminal, clock and kernel events
features.apple: Socket Event Types, Pseudoterminal Event Types, Clock Event Types, Kernel Event Types
features.note: No event hooks for these. The terminal app exists but emits no security events.

features.apple: es_mute_process, es_mute_path, es_mute_process_events, es_mute_path_events, es_unmute_*, es_clear_cache (Muting Events, Unmuting Events, Managing Cached Results)
features.note: Wave 2 (theme-20, parity/integration e52c2fd0): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. Depends on a client, which does not exist.

features.apple: es_retain_message, es_release_message, es_message_t (Retaining and Releasing Messages)
features.note: Message lifetime is a C memory-management detail. Rust ownership would cover it once an event API exists, so this is not a feature to build.
An Apple signing entitlement for system extensions. BifrOSt grants app permissions from its own manifests, and no signing-based entitlement applies.

gaps: No system-level security event client: nothing connects to the kernel or the shell to receive process, file and session events.
No authorization hook: nothing can allow or deny an exec, open or mount before it happens.
Process events are limited to app launch and terminate from the shell; no exec arguments, environment, file descriptors, parent chain or processes outside the shell.
File events are content changes only, with no process attribution and no metadata, xattr or ACL events.
No mount, memory-mapping, ptrace, remote-thread, credential-change or code-signing events.
Login, sudo, SSH and screen-sharing sessions are logged but not published as events.
docs/bifrost-ui.md names the file watcher FSEventStream in bifrost_app::fsevents, but the code is springboard/sdk/src/fswatch.rs (WatchStream). The docs need correcting.
